conventions.convention: Inner products and Hermitian sesquilinear forms are linear in the first argument. Matrix entries are G_ij = ⟨φ_j,φ_i⟩ and A_ij = q(φ_j,φ_i).

Conforming trial vectors belong to the form domain Q; membership in the associated operator domain is not required. The procedure uses exact matrix entries and supplies no enclosure for quadrature or eigensolver errors.

The essential spectrum excludes isolated eigenvalues of finite multiplicity; its empty-set infimum is +∞. Variational indices begin at 1, eigenvalues count multiplicity, and an empty variational family has infimum +∞.
Ritz convergence requires nested finite-dimensional spaces whose union is dense in the form norm, and is asserted for fixed k only when λ_k(A) is strictly below the essential-spectrum threshold.

A continuum residual uses a normalized u in D(T) and real λ. A selected Borel spectral set Δ needs a separate positive gap g from λ to every spectral point outside Δ; an empty spectral complement gives zero outside amplitude.

Propagation uses exp(−i(t−t₀)T/ℏ), ℏ > 0, and residual r = iℏv′−Tv. The path is C¹ into H, lies pointwise in D(T), and Tv is continuous; the final bound integrates over the unoriented interval between t and t₀.
Hermite eigenfunctions are indexed from j = 0, with E_j = ℏω(j+1/2); V_n contains ψ₀ through ψ_{n−1}. Parameters m, ω and ℏ are positive mathematical inputs.
The three theorems and both examples explicitly assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

load_bearing.statement: Assume Choice and Countable Choice. For nonzero complex H, self-adjoint A ≥ −cI, and finite-dimensional V contained in Q(A), θ_k(V) ≥ λ_k(A) for 1 ≤ k ≤ dim V. For nested finite-dimensional V_n with form-norm-dense union, θ_k(V_n) decreases to λ_k(A) whenever λ_k(A) < inf σ_ess(A), using +∞ for an empty essential spectrum and an empty variational family.

For a densely defined closed semibounded Hermitian form and n ≥ 1 independent trial vectors in its domain, form the exact Gram and form matrices G and A, diagonalize B = G^(−1/2) A G^(−1/2), order its eigenvalues ρ₁ ≤ ⋯ ≤ ρ_n with multiplicity, and return (ρ_j, G^(−1/2)y_j) for an orthonormal eigenbasis y_j.

Assume Choice and Countable Choice. For self-adjoint T on nonzero complex H, normalized u in D(T), real λ, r = (T−λI)u, and Borel Δ, if g > 0 and |x−λ| ≥ g on σ(T) outside Δ, then dist(λ,σ(T)) ≤ ‖r‖ and ‖(I−E_T(Δ))u‖ ≤ ‖r‖/g. An empty spectral complement gives zero outside amplitude.

Assume Choice and Countable Choice. Let T be self-adjoint on nonzero complex H, ℏ > 0, I an open interval, t₀ in I, v in C¹(I;H), v(s) in D(T), and Tv continuous. With r(s) = iℏv′(s)−Tv(s), for every t in I the norm of v(t)−exp(−i(t−t₀)T/ℏ)v(t₀) is at most ℏ^(−1) times the integral of ‖r(s)‖ between min(t,t₀) and max(t,t₀).

The consumer preserves self-adjointness, semiboundedness, choice assumptions, form domain, multiplicities, and essential-spectrum conventions. Its convergence claim is restricted to eigenvalues strictly below the threshold; the finite-subspace comparison and convergence argument are proved locally.

This is a reading-context page prerequisite, not an item-level invocation. The finite-level Duhamel supplier states finite-dimensional bounded-coupling estimates; the assigned propagation theorem independently proves its self-adjoint-operator residual bound using explicit domain regularity and published unitary-group and integration suppliers. Neither page states a converse dependency or transfers the finite-dimensional result to an unbounded coupling.
